chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from one of his companions who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote in a letter to one of the caliphs of the Banu Umayya:

And among what he has squandered is the jihad, which God — Mighty and Majestic — has preferred over all deeds, and has preferred its performer over all other workers with a preference in ranks, forgiveness, and mercy — because through it religion became manifest, through it religion is defended, and through it God purchased from the believers their souls and their wealth for paradise, a successful and triumphant transaction, stipulating upon them in it the preservation of the [divine] limits.

The first of these [limits] is the call from obedience to servants toward obedience to God — Mighty and Majestic —, and from worship of servants toward worship of God, and from the wilayah of servants toward the wilayah of God.

So whoever is called to the jizya and refuses shall be killed and his family taken captive; but the [true] call is not from obedience to a servant toward obedience to another servant like him. And whoever acknowledges the jizya shall not be exceeded against, nor shall his covenant be violated, and he shall be burdened with less than his capacity.

The fay' (war spoils) shall belong to the Muslims in general, not to any particular group. And if there is fighting and captives, conduct in that shall be according to his [the Prophet's] sira, and action in that shall be according to his sunnah from the religion.

Then he burdened the blind and the lame — those whom God, Mighty and Majestic, had already exempted, who cannot find what to spend on jihad — and he burdens those who are able with what they cannot bear.

Rather, [the correct system was that] the people of each garrison city would fight those adjacent to them, with justice maintained among them in military expeditions. But all of that has vanished, to the point that people have become two types: a hired man acting as mercenary after God's transaction, and an employer who fines his companion after God had excused him. The hajj was taken away and wasted, and the people were impoverished. So who is more crooked than the one who made this crooked? And who is more upright than the one who set this upright? He imposed jihad upon the servants while cutting off [the support of] jihad from the servants — that is indeed a grave error.

key_terms.البعوث: Bu'uth — military expeditions/deployments; the system of equitable rotation among garrison towns
key_terms.الجزية: Jizya — the poll-tax levied on non-Muslim subjects under Islamic governance (dhimmis) in lieu of military service
key_terms.الجهاد: Jihad — striving in the way of God; here encompasses both armed struggle and its proper institutional framework
key_terms.الذمة: Dhimma — the covenant of protection extended to non-Muslim subjects; 'تُخْفَر الذمة' means to violate that covenant
key_terms.الفيء: Fay' — war spoils/revenues from non-combat acquisition; belongs to the Muslim community collectively
key_terms.الولاية: Wilayah — guardianship, authority, loyalty; here contrasted between divine wilayah (proper) and human wilayah (improper)
key_terms.حفظ الحدود: Preservation of the [divine] limits — adherence to the boundaries God established in matters of jihad
key_terms.عزّ وجلّ: Mighty and Majestic — honorific for God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the Umayyad corruption of jihad?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) wrote a letter to an Umayyad caliph critiquing the regime's corruption of the institution of jihad. The Imam invokes the Quranic covenant (9:111) by which God purchased the believers' souls and wealth for paradise, establishing that the true purpose of jihad is calling people to obedience and worship of God — not political conquest for personal gain. He details how the Umayyad system violated Islamic norms: burdening the exempt, monopolizing war spoils, abandoning the just garrison-system, converting religious obligation into mere mercenary employment, neglecting hajj, and impoverishing the people — concluding that this constitutes a grave error.
